fgos-coding-implement.description:
code-implement work for the coding domain's executing stage -- pinned to gemini-3.6-flash-medium via this capability's own providerModel/rigorOverrides (agy/gemini, lightweight policy tier; see modelPolicies.gemini.lightweight for the literal model string).

Flipped to executors.agy-herdr on 2026-09-07, which is the condition the previous description set: "do not flip prefer back to agy-herdr until this is fixed and re-verified live". Both halves of the old failure are gone, and gone structurally rather than by tuning.

The prompt no longer travels on a command line at all -- it is written to brief-<round>.md and only a one-line pointer is submitted -- so the multi-line corruption that used to destroy every real implement prompt has nowhere left to happen. Completion is now the worker's own outbox/result-<round>.json appearing; agent_status is never read as completion, which is what produced the silent false successes (idle before the agent had started; an idle-looking gap mid-turn).

Evidence: 10/10 settled with ack and result (P1, 2026-09-07), plus 2/2 again driven from this very config entry after the -i flag was removed from its args -- that flag made agy take the NEXT flag as its prompt value and never reach ready. Logs: docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/visibility-herdr/proofs/2026-09-07-v0/.

Bounded honestly: every one of those rounds ran a trivial task with a six-line prompt. What is proven is contract conformance -- agy reads the pointer, finds the brief, writes ack/report/result -- not that agy does hard implementation work well. The first real fgos-coding-implement dispatch is the real test.

Reverting is one field: set prefer back to "agy-cli". A failure now leaves a named outcome (agent_not_ready, agent_prompt_stalled, agent_blocked, died, timed-out-idle, timed-out-ceiling, paused-limit), an open pane with the reason still on screen, and a run.json that says settled/died/unknown instead of sitting at running forever -- so a bad flip is visible within one dispatch rather than silently burning a timeout window.

claude-reviewer.description: Claude Code CLI, scoped for a READ_ONLY_ROLES (reviewer/researcher/advisor) Assignment (Cell 6.3 Fix Round 1, Red-team finding): identical to executors.claude except it drops the git-write grant (Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*),Bash(rtk git add:*),Bash(rtk git commit:*)) and the --allowedTools flag entirely -- a reviewer never had a legitimate need for any Bash grant, and dropping the flag leaves only the CLI's own built-in read-only Bash allowlist (git status/diff/log-class commands), never write-capable ones. --permission-mode acceptEdits is kept so the reviewer can still Write its own agent-result.json/agent-report.md into its own run dir (proven live in Cell 6.3) -- this is a tool-family gate (no git-write for ANY path), not real path-scoping: Claude Code only consults path rules written as Edit(path)/Read(path) (a Write(path) rule is accepted but never consulted -- code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions), and this executor's args are a static config-time template with no per-run runDir substitution today, so an Edit(<runDir>/**) rule cannot be wired without adding a new templating dimension -- out of this fix round's scope (see docs/architect/agent-coordination/trace/step-06-cell-3-validate-plan-live-smoke.md's Fix Round 1 section for the accepted residual).

codex-readonly.description: RETIRED FOR DISPATCH -- do not bind this executor to any role. `-s read-only` has no writable-exception mechanism, so a dispatched agent can never write the agent-result.json that assignment-runner.mjs requires; every dispatch settles `no-evidence` regardless of how good the agent's actual findings were. Confirmed live (a real advisory panel dispatch failed this way and had to be retried on another executor) and by probe: `-s read-only --add-dir <dir>` still grants no write, which matches the CLI's documented design (--add-dir is meaningful only under workspace-write). Use codex-bwrap instead -- same provider family, OS-level confinement, and a real write path for its own result. Kept registered only so existing references resolve and this explanation stays discoverable. OpenAI Codex CLI under its own provider-native read-only sandbox (-s read-only) -- the read-only-confined pair for architecture-advisory-panel dispatch (tsk-1o4; live-proven safe P00.1: this flag blocked the same attack codex-cli's --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox let through, admitted to the allowlist; codex-bwrap, the OS-mount alternative, was excluded for a non-runnable startup crash, not a safety failure).
